definitions.name: read
definitions.description: Read a text file. Files are capped at 2000 lines / 50KB, and any single line longer than 500 characters is cut with a marker saying so; when either cap bites, the output ends with the exact offset=N to pass next. Prefer this over shelling out to `cat` — it is cheaper and it pages deterministically.

path.description: File path, relative to the working directory.

offset.description: First line to return, 1-based. Use the offset named in a truncation note to continue a large file.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Optional.

definitions.name: write
definitions.description: Create a file or replace its entire contents. Parent directories are created automatically. Overwrites without asking. Use for new files or deliberate whole-file rewrites; use edit to change part of an existing file.

path.description: File path, relative to the working directory.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.

definitions.name: edit
definitions.description: Replace an exact string in one file. old_string must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true; on zero or multiple matches nothing is written and the error says the count. CRLF line endings and a UTF-8 BOM are handled for you: quote the text as it looked when you read it. Prefer this over write for any change to part of a file.

path.description: File path, relative to the working directory.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace, including indentation. Keep it as small as possible while still unique in the file.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence. Defaults to false.

definitions.name: glob
definitions.description: List files and directories by name pattern, without reading any of them. Prefer this to ls, dir, fd or find in the shell: it is the same listing on every platform, it needs no quoting, and it starts the walk at the fixed part of the pattern instead of at the whole tree. Directories come back with a trailing slash, so a bare name lists what is in a directory. A doubled star crosses directories and a single star does not; a pattern with no slash in it also matches the file name, so *.ts reaches apps/cli/ui/parts.tsx. Results are sorted by path, and the number matched is always reported, so a capped list cannot read as a complete one. Skips .git and node_modules.

pattern.description: Glob to match paths against, e.g. "*.ts", "**/*.test.ts" or "apps/cli/src".

path.description: A directory to search. Defaults to the whole working directory.

head_limit.description: Stop after this many paths. Defaults to 100.

definitions.name: shell
definitions.description: Run a command in the user's shell, in the working directory. This is PowerShell, not bash: use cmdlets and PowerShell operators. `Get-ChildItem`, `Get-Content`, `Select-String`, `Test-Path` exist; `ls` and `cat` are aliases for two of them. `find` does NOT exist — use `Get-ChildItem`. Quote paths in single quotes. Chain commands with `&&`. Returns stdout and stderr, then the exit code on the last line. Use for git, listing, searching, package managers, test runners — everything that is not a plain read/write/edit of one file. No timeout by default; pass timeout (seconds, max 3600) for anything that could hang. Output is capped, keeping the tail where errors are.

timeout.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Optional; no default timeout.

definitions.name: task
definitions.description: Delegate a self-contained subtask to a sub-agent that runs with the same tools and endpoint and returns its final answer. Use it to keep long research or multi-step work out of this conversation's context; the sub-agent cannot see this conversation, so the prompt must contain everything it needs. It returns the sub-agent's answer, or a note that it produced none.

prompt.description: The complete task for the sub-agent, in full — it cannot see this conversation, so include all context, file paths and goals it needs.

description.description: A short label for what the sub-agent is doing, shown on the activity line.

definitions.name: skill
definitions.description: Load a skill's instructions by name. Skills are reusable playbooks; the system prompt lists their names and one-line descriptions, and this returns the full body to follow. Pass args to fill $ARGUMENTS in the body. Use it when a listed skill matches the task.

name.description: The skill's name, exactly as listed in the prompt.

args.description: Optional text substituted for $ARGUMENTS in the skill body.

definitions.name: rg
definitions.description: Search file contents with ripgrep and get back matching paths, matching lines with context, or match counts. Respects .gitignore and skips binaries. The pattern is a Rust regular expression (ripgrep syntax), not a glob. An include glob with no slash matches the file name, so *.ts reaches apps/cli/ui/parts.tsx. Prefer this to grepping in the shell.

pattern.description: Rust regular expression to search for.

path.description: A file or directory to search. Defaults to the whole working directory.

include.description: Only search paths matching this glob, e.g. "*.ts" or "apps/**/test.ts".

output_mode.description: matching paths (the default), matching lines with context, or the number of matching lines per file.

context.description: Lines either side of each match, for output_mode "content". Defaults to 0.

case_insensitive.description: Match without regard to case. Defaults to false.

multiline.description: Let the pattern cross line ends. Defaults to false.

head_limit.description: Stop after this many results. Defaults to 250.

definitions.description: Read a text file. Lines are 1-based; use offset and limit to select a range.

definitions.description: Search file contents using a regex or literal pattern.

path.description: File or directory, default workspace root

definitions.name: glob
definitions.description: Find files matching a glob pattern.

definitions.name: tree
definitions.description: Show the directory tree.

definitions.name: index
definitions.description: Query the repository index.

definitions.name: skill
definitions.description: Load a skill by name.

definitions.name: web_search
definitions.description: Search the web and return relevant results.

definitions.name: fetch
definitions.description: Fetch a URL and return its content as text.

definitions.name: edit
definitions.description: Replace exact text in an existing file.

all.description: Replace all matches instead of requiring a unique match

definitions.name: delete
definitions.description: Delete a file or directory.

definitions.description: Read-only local inspection. Pick op and supply that op's argument: read→path; grep→pattern (optional path, glob); glob→pattern (optional path); tree→path, depth (both optional); index→query; skill→name.

definitions.name: modify
definitions.description: Change one file. Pick op and supply that op's arguments: write→path + content; edit→path + old + new (optional all); delete→path.

definitions.name: web
definitions.description: Search the web or fetch a URL. op=search→query (optional limit); op=fetch→url.

definitions.name: act
definitions.description: Perform exactly one operation. Choose op and provide that operation's arguments.
